result.summary: Do not ship yet: reset tokens leak into HTTP log views, file-creation failures escape handling, and the exposed recovery flow cannot complete.

findings.title: Reset tokens enter the web-visible log buffer
findings.body: The new warning sends the token to every configured sink. triggarr/logging.py:72-84 stores it unredacted in log_buffer; /partials/log-viewer renders that buffer through templates/partials/log_viewer.html:80. A session or API-key holder can therefore retrieve the supposedly operator-only recovery secret over HTTP. Authentication guards the viewer, but does not enforce the intended filesystem/container-access boundary. This is newly exposed token data, not a pre-existing logging leak.
findings.recommendation: Mark recovery log records and exclude them from the web buffer while retaining them in the operator sink; test the log-viewer response after minting.

findings.title: Temporary-file creation bypasses non-fatal error handling
findings.body: mkstemp executes before the try block. A read-only config volume, permission failure, or exhausted disk therefore raises through run_in_executor and returns HTTP 500 after the token and rate-limit state have already been committed. An isolated execution with mkstemp raising PermissionError confirmed that the exception escapes and the error logger is never called.
findings.recommendation: Move temporary-file creation inside the protected block, initialize cleanup state safely, and test creation failures while preserving the log-based recovery response.

findings.title: The exposed reset flow has no token-consumption endpoint
findings.body: GET /reset/request now exposes a password-recovery form and POST mints a token, but the registered router contains no /reset/confirm handler or other reset-token consumer. The existing confirmation form targets /reset/confirm (templates/reset.html:29), which returns 404. Thus an operator can request and retrieve a token but cannot use it to recover access; the newly activated flow requires the missing consumer.
findings.recommendation: Implement and connect the confirmation flow before exposing these routes, or gate the entire recovery feature until it works end to end.

next_steps: Fix sink isolation and file-creation error handling.
Complete or gate recovery, then verify the full request-to-password-reset flow.
